answer: Duplicate identities can't split the bond without losing more than a dune loses sand to wind, so forging extra participants costs real capital. Each agent must stake a bond and solve a per-epoch proof tied to a rotating beacon seed, like water tracing a karst channel to its source. Peers verify the beacon signature before attesting, making cheap mass registration unprofitable. From once0010's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
